newsitem.title: UK: Ferry firms win injunction against French blockade.
newsitem.headline: Ferry firms win injunction against French blockade.

text.p: European ferry giants P&O, Stena Line AB and Sea France won an injunction in the French courts on Wednesday to end the blockade of ports at Dunkirk, Calais and Boulogne by protesting French fishermen.

A spokesman for Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co told Reuters "We've been granted an injunction. The injunction will be served by French civil servants in one hour and the fishermen are liable for personal fines of 10,000 francs ($1,730) per person for each hour they maintain the protest beyond the deadline," he said.
The P&O spokesman added that the French court hearing ended around 1530 GMT and said normal ferry services would resume once the fishermen cleared their protest.

French fishermen began the blockade on Tuesday, protesting against European Union regulations on net sizes. Their efforts have thrown the ferry services into chaos. The blockade has effected five P&O ferries, which have been diverted to Zeebruge, with three Stena ferries hit and three from Sea France.

The delay has hit thousands of holidaymakers as well as freight companies which are still unable to use the Channel Tunnel freight service, which remains closed following a fire last November, and is not due to reopen until mid-June.

"This has obviously had a tremendous financial impact," said a P&O spokeswoman earlier. The company later added that the cost could run to "thousands of pounds in lost revenues" but refused to quanify further.

John Hix, spokesman for the Freight Transport Association, told Reuters that the hit on its members was also sizeable. "We estimate the cost at 0.5 million to 0.75 million pounds ($1.2 million) a day. And there are probably between 1,200 to 1,500 trucks stuck this side of the Channel with a similar number in France." ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
